# Chrome native messaging

Fetched: 17/10/2026 from https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/develop/concepts/native-messaging, https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/develop/concepts/service-workers/lifecycle, https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/runtime, and Chromium source at `refs/heads/main` on chromium.googlesource.com: `chrome/browser/extensions/api/messaging/native_message_process_host.cc`, `chrome/browser/extensions/api/messaging/launch_context.cc`, `chrome/common/chrome_paths.cc`, `extensions/renderer/api/messaging/messaging_util.cc`, `extensions/browser/api/messaging/message_service.cc`, `extensions/browser/api/messaging/extension_message_port.cc`.
Version: docs as published on 17/10/2026; Chromium source at main on 17/10/2026; local browser Google Chrome 155.0.8059.80 (macOS).

## What this project uses

### Host manifest

Required fields: `name`, `description`, `path`, `type`, `allowed_origins`. Shape (from the docs example, names are placeholders):

```json
{
  "name": "com.my_company.my_application",
  "description": "My Application",
  "path": "/absolute/path/to/host-binary",
  "type": "stdio",
  "allowed_origins": ["chrome-extension://knldjmfmopnpolahpmmgbagdohdnhkik/"]
}
```

- `name`: "This name can only contain lowercase alphanumeric characters, underscores and dots." Cannot start or end with a dot, and no two consecutive dots.
- `path`: "On Linux and macOS the path must be absolute." The host starts with its working directory set to the folder containing the binary.
- `type`: "This parameter has one possible value: `stdio`."
- `allowed_origins`: list of extension origins allowed to use the host. "`allowed_origins` values _can't_ contain wildcards." Chrome checks the caller with `manifest->allowed_origins().MatchesSecurityOrigin(origin)` (`launch_context.cc`).

### Manifest location on macOS (Google Chrome)

- Per-user (default): `~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/NativeMessagingHosts/<name>.json`
- System-wide: `/Library/Google/Chrome/NativeMessagingHosts/<name>.json`
- Chromium uses `~/Library/Application Support/Chromium/NativeMessagingHosts/` and `/Library/Application Support/Chromium/NativeMessagingHosts/`. "In versions of Chrome earlier than Chrome 146, Google Chrome for Testing used the same locations as Google Chrome."

Shared by all profiles: the docs only say the per-user manifest lives under the user data directory's `NativeMessagingHosts/`. Source confirms it is resolved from the user data dir, not a profile dir (`chrome_paths.cc`):

```cpp
case chrome::DIR_USER_NATIVE_MESSAGING:
  if (!base::PathService::Get(chrome::DIR_USER_DATA, &cur)) { return false; }
  cur = cur.Append(FILE_PATH_LITERAL("NativeMessagingHosts"));
```

So one manifest serves every profile (`Default`, `Profile N`) of that user data dir. A different `--user-data-dir` has its own `NativeMessagingHosts/`.

Local check (read-only, 17/10/2026): `~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/NativeMessagingHosts/` exists and already contains `com.anthropic.claude_browser_extension.json` and `com.anthropic.claude_code_browser_extension.json` (plus a third-party host). Pick a distinct host name.

### Extension side

- Permission: `"nativeMessaging"`. "This permission is needed for connectNative(), sendNativeMessage() and onNativeConnect."
- `chrome.runtime.connectNative(application: string): Port`. "Connects to a native application in the host machine."
- `chrome.runtime.sendNativeMessage(application: string, message: object): Promise<any>` (promise form Chrome 99+).
- "These methods are not available inside content scripts, only inside your extension's pages and service worker."
- `Port.disconnect()`: "Immediately disconnect the port." "Calling disconnect() on an already-disconnected port has no effect."
- `Port.onDisconnect`: "Fired when the port is disconnected from the other end(s)." "This event is fired at most once." Read `chrome.runtime.lastError` inside the handler for the reason.

### Wire framing (stdio)

"Each message is serialized using JSON, UTF-8 encoded and is preceded with 32-bit message length in native byte order." Same format both directions. On Apple silicon and x86_64 Macs native order is little-endian (platform fact, not stated in the docs). Source reads the header as a raw `uint32_t` (`kMessageHeaderSize = 4`).

### How Chrome launches the host

- "Chrome starts each native messaging host in a separate process."
- `connectNative()`: Chrome keeps the host running "until the port is destroyed". One process per port: each `connectNative()` call spawns a new host process.
- `sendNativeMessage()`: a new process per message; the host's first message is the response and "All other messages generated by the native messaging host in that case are ignored."
- Arguments: first argument is the caller origin, `chrome-extension://[ID]/`. Source: "The origin must be the first argument" (`command_line.AppendArg(origin.spec())`).
- Windows only: `--parent-window=<decimal handle value>`; "this value will be 0 if the calling context is a service worker."
- Further args only in special cases (source): an error arg, or `--reconnect-command=<base64 JSON>` and `--native-messaging-connect-id=...` when the manifest supports native-initiated connections (the `onConnectNative` feature, which the runtime docs say "is only supported on Chrome OS"). The host is not told which profile launched it in the normal case; the origin is the only identity passed.

### Service worker lifetime while a native port is open

- Docs (lifecycle page, Chrome 105 entry): "Connecting to a native messaging host using browser.runtime.connectNative() will keep a service worker alive." "If the host process crashes or is shut down, the port is closed." The docs advise reconnecting from `onDisconnect`.
- The Chrome 116 entries on that page concern WebSockets only ("Active WebSocket connections now extend extension service worker lifetimes"). Nothing native-messaging-specific is listed for 116.
- Source (`message_service.cc`) for a native channel: `channel->opener->set_should_have_strong_keepalive(true); channel->opener->IncrementLazyKeepaliveCount(Activity::MESSAGE_PORT);` and `extension_message_port.cc` maps a strong keepalive to `ServiceWorkerExternalRequestTimeoutType::kDoesNotTimeout`. So while the port is open the worker is not stopped by the 30 s idle or 5 min request timers. The keepalive is released when the channel closes.

### Termination when the port disconnects

- Docs: not stated beyond "until the port is destroyed".
- Source (`NativeMessageProcessHost` destructor): "Kill the host process if necessary to make sure we don't leave zombies." On macOS it posts `base::EnsureProcessTerminated(process)` to a blocking thread pool. `Close()` also resets the read and write streams, so the host sees EOF on stdin. Design the host to exit on stdin EOF; Chrome will force-terminate it otherwise. Exact grace period: not stated in the docs.

## Errors

Strings from the docs (also present in source):

- "Failed to start native messaging host." Check execute permission of the binary.
- "Invalid native messaging host name specified." Name contains disallowed characters or dots.
- "Native host has exited." Pipe broke before Chrome read the message. Source: sent on EOF (`result == 0`) or `ERR_CONNECTION_RESET` while reading.
- "Specified native messaging host not found." Wrong name, wrong location, invalid JSON, or bad `path`. Source also logs "Found manifest, but not the binary for native messaging host" in this case.
- "Access to the specified native messaging host is forbidden." Origin not in `allowed_origins`.
- "Error when communicating with the native messaging host." Protocol violation. Source raises it when a host message exceeds 1 MB, or on any read/write error. "Keep stdout for protocol output only, use stderr for debugging."
- Extension to host message over 64 MiB, renderer side (`messaging_util.cc`): "Message exceeded maximum allowed size of 64MiB."

Debugging: launch Chrome with `--enable-logging=stderr --log-level=1` and grep `native_messag|launch_context`. Use `--log-level=1`, not `2`, which "suppresses these startup diagnostics".

## Limits

- Host to Chrome: "The maximum size of a single message from the native messaging host is 1 MB." Source: `constexpr size_t kMaximumNativeMessageSize = 1024 * 1024;` (1,048,576 bytes, compared against the length prefix, exclusive of the 4-byte header). Exceeding it closes the port.
- Chrome to host: "The maximum size of the message sent to the native messaging host is 64 MiB." Source comment: "IPC messages will fail at > 128 MiB. Restrict extension messages to 64 MiB."
- Number of concurrent ports or host processes: not stated.

## Gotchas

- 1 MB host-to-extension cap matters for screenshots and accessibility trees: anything sent from host to extension must be chunked, and anything big flowing from extension to host (base64 screenshots) has a 64 MiB ceiling.
- Every `connectNative()` spawns a fresh process, so a service worker restart (or a reconnect from `onDisconnect`) creates a new host process. Keep shared state in a separate long-lived daemon that each host process connects to.
- All profiles in one user data dir share the manifest and so the same host binary, but each profile's extension instance launches its own host process. The host only learns the extension origin, not the profile.
- `allowed_origins` has no wildcards: pin the extension ID with the manifest `key` field (see chrome-extension-apis.md).
- stdout is the protocol channel. Any stray print to stdout corrupts framing.
- macOS `path` must be absolute.
